cells.tense: You are picking the heading here, with a steady hand, at this hour.
cells.act: keep it at its real size when you are asked to shrink it
cells.ask: When someone wants less of you than you are, stay the size you are. Say your actual view once, plainly, and leave the sentence in the open.
cells.core:
Your aim and your ties run on the same fuel. You know what you're pointing at, and the people beside you are getting the unedited version of you, not a managed one. Being close to someone hasn't cost you your grip on where you're headed, and where you're headed hasn't made you hard to be near.

What to do with that is hold the line. When a gathering wants you smaller, stay whole and speak the sentence, even if it goes quiet for a minute. Pressing people to agree would be a different move, and you're not making it. Staying full-sized through the awkward stretch keeps this honest, and honesty among people is what keeps the direction firm without your having to fight for it.
cells.sheetLine: You're choosing, and the people are getting the real you.
cells.place: Where you feel with people and stay aligned

cells.tense: You will bend them toward the ending you already wrote down.
cells.act: look at the same thing longer, until it shows you more
cells.ask: Choose one person you keep angling toward a result. This week, put the plan down and study them instead — stay with looking well past where you'd normally move on.
cells.core:
Toward what you want, the steering has gotten past the hour you're in. You know where this should land, and your attention sits on the version that hasn't happened, so the actual human being across the table is being arranged toward it. You can feel the tightening in the air. Something that began as care now has a hand pressed down on it.

Nothing's wrong with wanting a certain ending. The way off it is to study the person longer than you study the plan, until they show you something you hadn't accounted for. Stop pushing the result for a stretch and notice who is actually here. The aim doesn't vanish when the hand loosens. It gets sharper, because now it's pointed at something real.
cells.sheetLine: Your grip is running past the person across from you.

cells.tense: You quit reaching toward them long back and assume nothing shifts.
cells.act: do one thing today the way only you do it, and do not explain it
cells.ask: With someone today, do something in your own particular manner — a phrase, a gesture, a call — and offer no explanation for it. Then remain for a bit.
cells.core:
Among people, your reach has gone still. You're present but not arriving, sitting at the edge while connection happens around you without your taking a chair. You don't expect it to be otherwise. What you're built to do hasn't gone anywhere — it's just been parked.

Don't try to push warmth into the numb spot. Let what you already are come out in something small instead: your own particular stamp on a single act, no apology attached. Do one such thing today with somebody and don't account for it. You don't have to feel close first. Do the thing in your own way, and closeness has a ledge to land on.
cells.sheetLine: You're here, but you've quit reaching toward anyone.
cells.place: Where you feel with people and stay aligned

cells.tense: You are steering a bond you would swear you are only riding.
cells.act: put your own name on what is already yours
cells.ask: Catch one move you make that shapes how things go with someone. Take a breath, own it as your move, and then either follow through or leave it.
cells.core:
A direction runs through your bonds and your hands are on the wheel, but you'd tell anyone it's just how things are. You've shown up a certain way so long that the steering feels like the tide — go along, don't rock it. The steering is real. The story you tell about it leaves the steering out.

The direction doesn't need changing. Just own the wheel. Next time some small move of yours tilts how things go with someone, take a beat, mark it as yours, and then either follow through or leave it. Naming it doesn't make you answerable for everything. It makes you the author of this, which you already were.
cells.sheetLine: You're shaping this, and calling it just how it is.
cells.place: Where you feel with people and stay aligned

attempts.check: The draft's one unsupported claim would be that any specific relationship is currently being forced or drifted through; the record gives only the capacity's state, not the person's situation, so every cell stays on what choosing looks like in this seat rather than naming who or what it involves. A reasonable objection is 'I'm not doing this to anyone' — the ask must stand alone as something the person could do about how they connect, not a verdict on a bond. The ask survives a wrong read because each is a single, self-contained act the person can do for their own sake: hold a position, look longer, do one thing the way only they do it. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person would be any line implying the reader is manipulating someone who hasn't asked for it — cut it, and keep every claim a condition of one capacity in one part of life.
